nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of precursor
nodes.procedure: A homogeneous solution was formed by mixing RuCl₃, boric acid (H₃BO₃) and GO solution using deionized water as the solvent, which was then reacted in a Teflon autoclave at 180°C for 12 h to obtain the precursor sample.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM and TEM reveal ~2.2 nm Ru_C uniformly grown on B-O/rGO support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and TEM images revealed that the ∼2.2 nm Ru_C was grown on the B-O/rGO support uniformly (Figures 1b and S4a,b).

nodes.characterization_summary: SR-XRD patterns show Ru (101) peak at 19.28° for Ru_C-B-O/rGO with negative shift of 0.41° relative to Ru_C-O/rGO at 19.48° due to B doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The synchrotron radiation X-ray diffraction (SR-XRD) patterns indicated that the Ru_C-B-O/rGO, Ru_C-B/rGO, and Ru_C-O/rGO catalysts exhibited two main peaks near 11.71° and 19.28°, respectively, corresponding to rGO (002) and Ru (101) crystal plane, as shown in Figure 2a.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru_C-B-O/rGO has BET surface area of 339.9 m² g⁻¹ with average pore size ~1.2 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of the Ru_C-B-O/rGO compound was 339.9 m² g⁻¹ with an average pore size of ∼1.2 nm (Figure S3).

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows ~2.2 nm Ru_C uniformly grown on B-O/rGO support and mainly exposes (101) crystal plane confirmed by diffraction spots and transformed plots.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) and TEM images revealed that the ∼2.2 nm Ru_C was grown on the B-O/rGO support uniformly (Figures 1b and S4a,b). ... Further, HAADF-STEM and diffraction spot images showed that Ru_C mainly exposed the (101) crystal plane (Figure S5).

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS mapping shows positions of B/O elements partially overlap with Ru elements, indicating successful B/O coordination with Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS) mapping and energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping of Ru_C-B-O/rGO show that the positions of B/O elements and those of Ru elements partially overlap, indicating the successful coordination of B/O with Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES absorption edges of Ru_C-B-O/rGO, Ru_C-B/rGO, and Ru_C-O/rGO highly coincident with Ru foil, indicating metallic Ru characteristics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES spectrum of Ru K edge indicated that the absorption edges of Ru_C-O/rGO, Ru_C-B/rGO, and Ru_C-B-O/rGO were highly coincident with the absorption edge of Ru foil, suggesting that Ru has typical metallic characteristics (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ru-B peak at 1.56 Å, Ru-O at 1.47 Å, and Ru_C-B-O/rGO characteristic peak at 1.50 Å (intermediate bond length); fitting shows Ru bonded to one O and three B atoms.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-EXAFS spectrum of Ru_C-B/rGO and Ru_C-O/rGO indicates that the dominant peak was located at 1.56 and 1.47Å, attributed to the bonding of Ru with B and O, respectively. The characteristic peak of the Ru_C-B-O/rGO was displayed at 1.50Å ... The fitting results presented in Table S1 provide additional evidence.

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS Ru 3p shows Ru⁰ peak 0.4 eV negative shift in Ru_C-B/rGO vs Ru_C-B-O/rGO; B 1s shows B-Ru bond at 188 eV with 0.6 eV positive shift in Ru_C-B/rGO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS peak position of Ru⁰ in Ru_C-B/rGO exhibits a 0.4 eV negative shift relative to Ru_C-B-O/rGO, suggesting that the electron density of Ru_C-B/rGO is low (Figure 2b). The B 1s orbital analysis reveals that the B—Ru bond emerges at 188 eV. Moreover, the B—Ru bond in Ru_C-B/rGO has a 0.6 eV positive shift compared with Ru_C-B-O/rGO (Figure 2c).

nodes.characterization_summary: O K-edge shows peaks at 531.6, 534.1, 539.4 eV indicating O occupies octahedral sites around Ru via O 2p-Ru 4d hybridization; decreased O content with increased B.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The results indicate that O occupies the octahedral sites surrounding Ru. Specifically, the two sharp characteristic peaks at 531.6 and 534.1 eV can be ascribed to the excitation of O 1s core electrons into the mixed state of t₂g and eg orbitals formed by the hybridization between O 2p and Ru 4d.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows significantly lower Ru content in Ru_C-B-O/G compared to other catalysts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Besides, inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES) tests indicate that the ratio of Ru in Ru_C-B-O/G was significantly lower compared with other catalysts (Table S2).
